## Assistant (started 2026-10-28T16:27:55.585Z)

    The architecture broadly fits the repository, but I found **10 actionable design gaps**, all **P2: fix before implementing the affected phase**. VT0 remains the right next step.
    
    1. **Chunk joining can delete real spoken words.** The plan cuts non-overlapping chunks, then removes matching words across their boundary. “No … no, start again” can lose a genuine occurrence. Deduplicate only overlapping observations of the same source interval. [Chunk merge](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/Feature plans/VO tab plan.md:315>)
    
    2. **Suggested keepers are not clearly separated from approved cuts.** Keepers start preselected, while rendering consumes kept spans without an explicit review barrier. An untouched “sure” row could therefore discard alternatives, contradicting “nothing is cut unreviewed.” Store suggestions and confirmed decisions separately; validate acceptance before rendering. [Takes board](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/Feature plans/VO tab plan.md:352>)
    
    3. **Re-analysis can invalidate saved editorial decisions.** Changing the engine or pause threshold can split and regroup takes, but the session model defines no analysis revision, stable span identities, or reconciliation rule. Add revision checks, explicit review invalidation, and a frozen input revision for rendering. [Session model](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/Feature plans/VO tab plan.md:406>)
    
    4. **Render recovery can publish twice.** A crash after inserting clips but before completing the job causes a retry. A deterministic seed does not provide operation-level idempotency. Define a persistent publication operation ID and transactional asset/session/clip registration. [Publication](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/Feature plans/VO tab plan.md:366>); [existing recovery precedent](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/apps/web/src/job-runners.ts:255>).
    
    5. **The proposed permissions cannot complete the full workflow.** Rendering requires `editSound`, but registering its output and assigning bins require `editMedia`. A custom sound-editing role can start work it cannot finish. Specify the complete capability contract or a narrowly authorized composite operation. [Proposed gates](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/Feature plans/VO tab plan.md:356>); [actual command permissions](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/packages/db-contracts/src/roles.ts:643>).
    
    6. **Practice-film protection is missing.** Learners have editing authority, so role checks alone would permit server-side session writes and transcription jobs on the shared practice film. Require `refusePracticeFilm` before those effects. [Proposed gates](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/Feature plans/VO tab plan.md:356>); [existing invariant](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/apps/web/src/practice-film.ts:13>).
    
    7. **VO-first placement depends on an unbuilt prerequisite.** Current audio placement refuses projects without an active animatic—even when a project frame rate exists. AC1 owns relaxing that guard, but VT5 promises placement upstream of AC1. Move that prerequisite into VT5 or explicitly defer placement. [VT5](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/Feature plans/VO tab plan.md:429>); [current refusal](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/packages/planner-domain/src/commands.ts:6747>).
    
    8. **Sample-accurate output lacks a frame-based placement contract.** Millisecond trims and gaps produce boundaries that existing `AudioClip` frame indices cannot represent exactly. Define an output-span manifest and rounding/padding policy so individual lines neither lose samples nor contain their neighbour’s speech. [Render design](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/Feature plans/VO tab plan.md:362>); [clip timing model](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/packages/planner-domain/src/model.ts:475>).
    
    9. **Grouping misses ordinary late pickups.** A recording ordered `A, B, C, A pickup, B pickup` cannot map correctly through the prescribed monotone script alignment or adjacency-only clustering. Add repeated-pass support or manual reassignment to the initial review workflow. [Grouping](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/Feature plans/VO tab plan.md:334>)
    
    10. **Speaker identities cannot be merged unchanged across chunks.** Independent requests can assign “speaker 0” to different people. The runner needs reconciliation or explicitly chunk-scoped identities before analysis uses speaker changes. [Merge design](<E:/YH_Tools/YHAP/Feature plans/VO tab plan.md:313>); [Deepgram’s documented label assignment](https://github.com/deepgram/recipes/blob/main/recipes/python/speech-to-text/v1/diarize/README.md).
    
    Reviewed the full plan, relevant code and related plans, plus selected official provider documentation. **No files changed.** Actual transcription fidelity and editing-time improvement still need the proposed VT0 measurements.

    **You need the system to recognize repeated attempts at the same intended line.** It should follow the recording’s sequence: narrator starts a line, stops or rephrases it, tries again, then continues. Scanning the whole file means finding these sequences everywhere in the recording.
    
    I made the previous implementation too broad. Its tests established processing coverage and responsiveness, but did not establish useful retake detection.
    
    I inspected the current file’s saved transcript and actual search results. These are transcript-backed examples; the times below are approximate ASR timestamps, and I haven’t listened to judge performance quality.
    
    | Location | What appears in the recording | What the system should recognize |
    |---|---|---|
    | **01:56–02:07** | “painfully hand cranks **his** turret” → “painfully hand cranks **the** turret trying to bring the tiger into sight” | Partial attempt followed by a fuller retry. |
    | **02:37–02:57** | “the gunner’s hydraulic traverse is far **faster**” → “The tiger gunner’s hydraulic traverse is far **quicker** than Orlovski’s hand crank…” | Reworded attempt at the same passage, with a longer continuation. |
    | **06:19–06:26** | “…the Soviet guns.” → “The Soviet guns.” → “Sorry.” → “The Soviet guns.” | Three attempts at a phrase; “Sorry” is intervening commentary. |
    | **08:38–08:48** | “But both **men** have seen strange things in this war…” → “But both **tank commanders** have seen strange things in this war…” | Two complete versions of the same line. |
    | **12:48–12:56** | “…continue **on** their grim work.” → “…continue **on with** their grim work.” | Immediate retry with a small wording change. |
    | **13:16–13:19** | “How has this happened?” twice | A likely two-take group, subject to listening confirmation. |
    | **22:46–24:20** | “They’ll never take him alive” appears four times, separated by discussion about the wording and animation. | One retry sequence spanning commentary. Within that passage, “He reaches for his pistol” and “Moroz pulls his pistol” are another possible rephrasing pair. |
    
    The last example matters: **nearby should be a strong preference, not an absolute time cutoff.** Discussion can separate attempts.
    
    The current algorithm has three concrete problems:
    
    - **It accepts topic similarity as evidence of a retake.** The existing semantic threshold corresponds to cosine similarity ≥0.46. The opening narration is grouped with unrelated later battle descriptions scoring approximately 0.46–0.48. They share tanks, combat and characters, but occupy different places in the story.
    - **Its candidates often have the wrong boundaries.** It generates overlapping word windows, and repeated-word anchors can interrupt sentence candidates. Of ten attempt boundaries I checked above, six were absent as intact candidates. The first displayed group even includes narration and spoken editorial discussion in the same candidate.
    - **It ignores recording sequence when establishing matches.** About 89% of returned candidate links connect intervals more than a minute apart. Drawing all those overlapping intervals produces the carpet of highlights in your screenshot.
    
    Research points toward a combined approach. Speech-repair detection distinguishes an abandoned fragment, optional intervening commentary, and its replacement; research uses wording patterns together with acoustic/prosodic cues to locate those boundaries. That fits this recording’s false starts and “Sorry” passages. [Speech-repair research](https://www.isca-archive.org/eurospeech_2003/liu03b_eurospeech.html)
    
    My recommended adjustment is:
    
    1. **Identify plausible spoken attempts first.** Use clauses, pauses, restart cues and surrounding context. Preserve complete lines while allowing partial retries within them. A pause alone should not define a take.
    2. **Compare neighboring attempts within a retry sequence.** Scan throughout the file, but prioritize the next few attempts. Allow intervening commentary and stronger evidence for later pickups.
    3. **Compare intended meaning and passage coverage.** Distinguish a complete alternative, a partial restart, a wording correction, a continuation and unrelated speech. Shared subject matter alone must be insufficient. Changed names, numbers or negation should be flagged for review because they may be the correction being recorded.
    4. **Use embeddings to propose candidates, then verify the pairs.** Keep the existing local model initially; evaluate a semantic-similarity cross-encoder for difficult pairs. Cross-encoders examine both texts together, which is the documented second stage for filtering retrieval results. It still needs calibration on actual retakes. [Retrieve and re-rank](https://www.sbert.net/examples/sentence_transformer/applications/retrieve_rerank/README.html), [semantic-similarity model](https://huggingface.co/cross-encoder/stsb-roberta-base)
    5. **Present one group per retry sequence.** Show its attempts in recording order, their differences and complete/partial status. Use compact overview markers and detailed highlighting for the selected group.
    
    This also matches the editing task described by existing retake tools: detecting repeated attempts at a line. Their published product descriptions do not disclose enough to copy their algorithms. [Descript’s retake workflow](https://feedback.descript.com/changelog/new-ai-action-remove-retakes)
    
    **I would first validate the revised detector against these passages and nearby unrelated battle sentences.** Success means recovering coherent take groups, rejecting topical lookalikes, and placing useful boundaries—not maximizing match count. That small evaluation should precede another full-file run.

## Assistant (started 2026-11-13T17:06:02.716Z)

    We have **basic warning heuristics, but no general model that understands narrator comments yet**. A fully local solution is feasible on an 8–12 GB GPU, using separate text and audio analysis.
    
    Today’s implementation has:
    
    - **Comment flags:** four exact directions, such as “one more time” and “from the top”.
    - **Retake filtering:** recognises some editorial discussion so it does not become a retake candidate.
    - **Mistake suggestions:** repeated words/phrases, incomplete restarts, fillers, low transcription confidence and timing warnings.
    - **Audio warnings:** possible clipping and unusual energy transients.
    
    These are provisional suggestions. The current semantic embeddings help compare takes; they do not reliably distinguish narration from discussion. See [current text detectors](C:/Users/DANIL-GODLEVSKII/.codex/worktrees/vo-reconcile-gate/YHAP/packages/planner-domain/src/vo/flags.ts).
    
    For understanding comments, these are practical local candidates:
    
    | Model | Hardware fit | Role I would test |
    |---|---|---|
    | **Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507**, quantized | Comfortable starting point for 8 GB | Fast classification of narration, comments and false starts |
    | **Qwen3-8B**, Q4_K_M | Plausible on 8 GB with bounded context; more headroom on 12 GB | Main candidate for contextual classification |
    | **Qwen3.5-9B**, 4-bit | Candidate for 12 GB | Compare against the 8B model for difficult passages |
    
    The publishers provide local model weights; Qwen3-8B also has an official GGUF distribution and llama.cpp instructions. **Hardware fit is an engineering estimate, not a measurement on your server**: context length, runtime and other GPU processes affect memory. None is yet validated for our recordings. [4B model](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507), [8B local distribution](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-8B-GGUF), [9B model](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B).
    
    I would give the model a passage with surrounding context, available script text and existing retake relationships. It would return **exact transcript word ranges**, a category and a short explanation:
    
    - Narration.
    - Recording direction: “Let me do that again.”
    - Editorial discussion: “We should use another word here.”
    - Abandoned attempt or self-correction.
    - Uncertain.
    
    Context matters: “The gun sounds horrible” might be narration or a comment about the recording. Script mismatch alone must not classify it as unrelated speech. These results should appear as **reviewable annotations**, separate from our green Keep/yellow Cut decisions.
    
    For gaps and short mistakes, I would use this combination:
    
    | Problem | Detection approach | Important limit |
    |---|---|---|
    | Long pauses, leading/trailing gaps | **Silero VAD** plus measured audio energy | Non-speech can contain breaths, room tone or intentional pauses |
    | Hesitations and abandoned starts | Transcript patterns plus contextual LLM classification | ASR sometimes removes stutters from its transcript |
    | Missing, extra or substituted words | Align each attempt with the script or another take | A wording difference can be intentional |
    | Clicks, pops, clipping, dropouts | Targeted audio signal detectors | Strong consonants can resemble transients |
    | Suspected mispronunciation | Targeted re-transcription/alignment of flagged audio | Neither alignment nor ASR confidence proves a pronunciation error |
    
    **Silero VAD runs locally on CPU**, leaving GPU capacity for transcription and text analysis. WhisperX is another local option for improving word alignment; its documentation describes wav2vec2 alignment and a transcription configuration below 8 GB GPU memory. Alignment improves localisation, but does not establish that the spoken word was correct. [Silero VAD](https://github.com/snakers4/silero-vad), [WhisperX](https://github.com/m-bain/whisperX).
    
    My recommendation is **Qwen3-8B Q4 for comments, Silero VAD for gaps, and the existing acoustic detectors for technical faults**. Run GPU stages sequentially. Validate against a small labelled set from the current recording—including legitimate narration that sounds like commentary—and re-transcribe only suspicious snippets. That gives us useful highlighting without repeatedly running expensive full-file analysis or automatically deleting uncertain material.

## Assistant (started 2026-11-13T17:16:21.314Z)

    Currently, **we have a pause threshold, but it splits take proposals rather than cutting pauses**.
    
    The workflow today is:
    
    1. **Pause (seconds)** defaults to **0.7 s**. Analysis checks gaps between transcription tokens and uses that threshold to separate takes.
    2. Audio between those takes becomes **Untranscribed audio** in Review & output.
    3. You audition those spans, mark them **Cut**, accept the review and render. A span can also be split manually to retain part of it.
    
    That explains the friction: there’s **no dedicated “find pauses longer than X” list, duration filter or bulk shortening action**. Smaller gaps can remain inside takes. Changing the analysis threshold also affects take segmentation, which is unnecessary for pause cleanup.
    
    We already use FFmpeg’s **silencedetect** when preparing transcription chunks—currently at **−40 dB**—but those results are not exposed as editable pause candidates. The output setting **Inter-part gap** adds spacing between kept parts; it does not detect or shorten existing pauses.
    
    For this task, we can start much simpler than an LLM or new GPU model:
    
    **Find pauses longer than [1.5 s] → highlight matches → audition → shorten selected pauses to [0.4 s].**
    
    I’d give that operation its own duration and silence-level controls, preserve speech margins, show the total time removed and support undo. It should work independently of retake analysis. Existing FFmpeg detection can supply the first candidates; VAD can later help distinguish quiet speech from non-speech.
    
    No code changed in this check.
